intent.summary: Groomed plans produced by the autonomous loop could lack the `## Fire-Disposition` section doctrine mika#1574 requires when a plan ships a detector-class deliverable. The architect then returns ITERATE correctly, and the grooming loop — which has exactly ONE iteration — spends it on a purely formal defect; at the second pass the gate has no recourse, so the ticket ESCALATEs and implementation is never dispatched. The change adds (a) `_FIRE_DISPOSITION_RULE`, a prescription constant injected into the grooming pilot's PROMPT conditional on SKILL=dev-groom, and (b) `_fd_retry_if_section_still_missing`, a one-shot retry of the revise pilot when the first-pass findings asked for the section and the revised plan still lacks it. The architect call budget (two passes) must be unchanged, and the retry must never refuse anything — it retries once, then lets the plan through while logging.

requirements: R1 — every grooming pilot dispatched by the autonomous loop receives, in the channel the substrate controls, the prescription to emit `## Fire-Disposition` when the plan ships a detector deliverable.
R2 — a revise launched on a finding demanding `## Fire-Disposition` can no longer report converged while the section is still absent.
R3 — the architect budget (two passes) is UNCHANGED. No additional `_arch_ask` call.
R4 — the nominal path (plan with no detector, or plan already carrying the section) pays nothing: no call, no branch, no log line.
R5 — any unreadable information takes the dispatch OUT of the treated population rather than into it (house fail-safe direction).
R6 — what is not deliverable in this repo is NAMED, not simulated.
implementation_units: U1 — dispatch-lib.sh: constant `_FIRE_DISPOSITION_RULE` beside `_PR_BODY_CONTAINMENT_RULE`, injected into PROMPT after it, conditional on SKILL=dev-groom.

U2 — dispatch-lib.sh: inside `_launch_revise_pilot`'s sha256-changed branch, when the first-pass findings file received as $1 demanded Fire-Disposition and the revised plan still lacks `^## Fire-Disposition`, write a targeted findings file and relaunch the revise pilot ONCE. Direct invocation, never recursion into `_launch_revise_pilot`.
U2b — termination: after the second attempt the section is re-tested FOR LOGGING ONLY, never to loop.
U3 — dispatch-lib.sh: an explicit guard counter `_FD_REVISE_RETRIED`, reset at entry to `_launch_revise_pilot`.
U4 — test-dispatch-lib.sh: the eleven tests T1–T11.
U5 — docs/solutions/best-practices/fire-disposition-doctrine.md: a `Site de production` section naming the two production sites and the mika-platform follow-up.
settled_decisions: D1 (session-settled: user-directed) — the prescription site is the PROMPT built by dispatch-lib, NOT the three grooming slash commands: those live in senara-solutions/mika-platform and are seeded into the worktree by `_seed_worktree_slash_commands` (mika#1415), so a ticket on senara-solutions/mika cannot edit them. Precedent twenty lines away: `_PR_BODY_CONTAINMENT_RULE` (mika#2211).

D2 (session-settled: user-approved) — a deterministic CI guard in verify-pipeline.sh is REFUSED on three measured grounds: it would run after the authority it contradicts (grooming opens no PR, so CI sees the plan only at the implementation PR, after the architect said GROOMED); the conditionality is not expressible in bash (whether a plan ships a detector is the semantic judgement mika#1574 delegates to an LLM, and making the section unconditional would contradict the doctrine's own `gate is N/A` branch); and it would move the blockage one gate further without lifting it. Do NOT propose adding that guard.
D3 (session-settled: user-approved) — what is widened is the REVISE budget (an implementation detail no document prescribes), never the ARCHITECT budget (two passes, mika#1271 design).

D4 (session-settled: user-directed) — the predicate's first term reads the FIRST-PASS findings file received as $1 and NEVER the targeted `findings-1-fd.md` the guard writes itself: that file contains the trigger string by construction, so reading it would make the predicate self-sustaining and true always. Corollary: the relaunch is a direct pilot invocation, never a recursion into `_launch_revise_pilot`, since recursion would make the written file become `$1` on the second turn.

D5 (session-settled: user-approved) — the prescription is conditional on SKILL=dev-groom. The neighbouring injection site is unconditional and correct for itself; the condition here must be written explicitly, not inherited.
